The client email (item ii) instructs acceptance on that condition. Corrigan's transmittal describes this as 'adding' affiliates, which overstates the change against the base.

limits: This review is decision support for the lawyer. It does not accept, reject, sign or send anything. The task instruction to 'accept, reject, or partially accept' each change and to produce counter-turn-redline.docx and cover-note.docx was not carried out; outcomes remain the lawyer's call.

Client instructions in email-sung-to-orenbach-review-request.eml were treated as taking precedence over general playbook tiers, and are cited in each affected finding. Most coincide with playbook positions. Where the playbook would require escalation (industry carve-out p37; good-faith disclaimer p105), the client's explicit instruction governed this review. project-lantern-timeline.xlsx was treated as a deal record, not as instructions; where its tracker marks Permitted Purpose 'Accept', the client email's request to evaluate and flag was followed.

Deleted paragraphs p72, p73, p74, p77, p78 (Residuals) and p118, p119, p120 (Delaware forum clauses) have empty current text, so no evidence could be quoted from them. They are addressed through p75, p76, p79, p114 and p117 for Residuals and Section 13 generally, and through p121–p123, which carry suggested restorations of the forum text. p75 and p76 contain only whitespace, so their evidence quotes are a single space.

Restoring the Residuals section (S-06 Hard Line; client item v) requires inserting several paragraphs, which single-paragraph suggested text cannot do. Restoration also requires reverting Corrigan's renumbering of Sections 6 and 7 and every cross-reference to them (p79–p85, p86, p95, p112–p114). No qualified residuals wording is supplied here, although S-06 §6.2 and the client email describe the trade-secret and 'Highly Confidential — No Residuals' qualifiers.

Several playbook descriptions of the 'v.6.2 form' do not match the supplied baseline text. Permitted Purpose wording, the standard-of-care phrasing, the 'competent documentary evidence' standard, compelled-disclosure costs, the jury waiver and the non-solicitation remedies all differ. Findings rely on the actual baseline text and note these differences where relevant.

Neither the corrigan-transmittal-email.eml nor the client email lists which edits are the six 'conforming/typographical' changes. Classification here is by inspection. The p41 proviso and p133 'conversion' insertion were not described by Corrigan and are flagged for the lawyer.

Deal-team confirmation required by S-04 (Permitted Purpose) has not been verified from the supplied materials. Neither has the S-01 instruction about using the project code name in the agreement. Confirmation of structural details of the Data Analytics Division (assets, contracts, personnel held elsewhere in Corrigan) is also not supplied.

Headers, footers, footnotes and endnotes were not reviewed (per import warning). Formatting artifacts in the imported text (markdown asterisks, HTML comments, embedded track-change markers) may not reflect the actual Word document.
No view is expressed on enforceability under Delaware or Virginia law, or on whether existing Section 2.5 alone satisfies the S-03 breach-responsibility condition. Those are judgments for the lawyer.
Privileged deal information in the context documents (valuation, financial advisor identity) was not used in any finding and should not appear in any external communication.
